quotes.text: three datasets from the MIMIC-IV database: the core MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2, and MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2
placeholders such as subject_id , hadm_id , or stay_id , which are populated when the scenario is instantiated

rationale: Dataset names, versions and platform (PhysioNet, in references) are given. Cases are tied to source records through subject_id, hadm_id and stay_id placeholders, and every verdict must cite the MIMIC-IV record span. The 2008-2019 time frame appears in Appendix B.

quotes.text: retrospective, de-identified records from the inpatient, intensive-care, and emergency departments of a single major academic medical center
The patient-linked artifacts, which are derived from MIMIC-IV, will be made available on PhysioNet under its credentialed access policy and data use agreement.

rationale: Origin (MIMIC-IV, real de-identified), collection nature (retrospective) and terms (PhysioNet credentialed access and DUA) are stated. No consent or IRB status, and no explicit 'not required', appears in the packet, so the top anchor is not met.

quotes.text: We sample 30 patients per scenario using stratification across Yes , No , and Indeterminate candidate strata

rationale: A stated sampling design (stratified, 30 per scenario) and database descriptive counts are given. The paper explicitly disclaims prevalence representativeness, and there is no comparison against a named target population.

quotes.text: Must-not criteria state prohibited shortcuts and unsupported inferences, such as inferring an endpoint from an administrative code alone

rationale: Borderline. Must-not criteria (process defects) and the over-commitment rate act as unsafe-output checks in a clinical audit frame, but they are not a dedicated harmful-output test. No bias or fairness test appears anywhere in the packet. Scored 1 for the unsafe-output side only.

quotes.text: run with web search and fetch disabled, so every system answers from the in-environment patient record and policy corpus alone
The patient-linked artifacts, which are derived from MIMIC-IV, will be made available on PhysioNet under its credentialed access policy and data use agreement.

rationale: Controls exist (web access disabled during runs, credentialed gated release of patient-linked data), but no canary, held-out split, encryption or measured overlap or contamination check is reported. A control without a measured check scores 1.

quotes.text: MIMIC data is reached only through a credential-isolated tool server, so no system can bypass the governed tools to read raw records.

rationale: Isolation of raw records is stated with a mechanism (credential-isolated tool server, web disabled), but the packet never says explicitly that agents cannot reach the reference verdicts. Scored 1 because the gold-isolation claim is only implicit.

quotes.text: the core MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2, and MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2
The production judge is GPT-5.5, which is itself among the evaluated systems

rationale: Data versions and a fixed policy corpus are pinned, and the judge model, prompt and rubric are held fixed. However, the judge is a live LLM call at evaluation time with no snapshot or date, and harness versions are not stated. Data pinned with a live or unpinned evaluator scores 1.

quotes.text: two clinicians independently vetted every scenario, confirming the query reflects a real chart-review workflow
the reference verdict matched the clinician verdict on 91% of cases with a defined label

rationale: No scripted reference solution is run through the grader. Solvability and correctness evidence is manual: clinician vetting of scenarios and clinician calibration of reference verdicts.

searched: S1 (tool environment 3.2, scenario anatomy, evaluation framework), S2-S5 (no chunks). Tools are retrieval, a capped read-only SQL interface, a sandboxed compute shell and a policy-document reader, and the agent returns a verdict report. No task changes environment state.

quotes.text: This intentional balancing prevents aggregate performance from being dominated by straightforward positive or negative cases

rationale: A design argument is stated: stratified balancing across Yes/No/Indeterminate, exact four-class match, macro-F1 and defect-free accuracy. No empirical random or trivial-agent rate or explicit chance rate is reported.
searched: S1 (results sections 6.2-6.7, appendices C-E, Tables 3-18), S2 (no chunks), S3 (no chunks), S4 (no chunks), S5 (no chunks). No do-nothing, random or majority-class agent score is reported.

quotes.text: they agree on 97.9% of 1,331 category decisions
the reference verdict matched the clinician verdict on 91% of cases with a defined label

rationale: The benchmark validates its own outputs with figures: regrading agreement (97.9%, kappa 0.95), a five-judge panel (16% of criteria contested, Fleiss kappa about 0.65), policy-judge kappa about 0.86, and reference verdicts against clinicians (91%, kappa 0.87). Judge independence is acknowledged as untested with an independent judge.

quotes.text: In our primary protocol each case is run once, giving a one-to-one correspondence between cases and runs
Each system has three independent attempts on all 148 cases.

rationale: A repeated-run policy exists only for a development subset (k=3), and headline runs are single attempts. No seed, temperature or other decoding control is stated in S1-S3, so only part of the safeguard is reported.

quotes.text: only 11 reach p<0.05 under a two-sided exact McNemar test and none survives Holm correction
binomial standard error bars at n=750

rationale: Paired exact McNemar tests with Holm correction are applied to the sixteen-system comparison (on the 148-case development subset), and SE bars are shown at n=750. The paper reports the tests as non-separating, which still counts as a test of the model comparison.

quotes.text: In our primary protocol each case is run once, giving a one-to-one correspondence between cases and runs
Each system has three independent attempts on all 148 cases.

rationale: Run counts are stated (1 per case for headline, 3 on the dev subset) and the attempts are described as independent. No seed, temperature or other decoding controls, and no statement that the API exposes none, appear in S1-S3. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: binomial standard error bars at n=750
formal comparisons should use paired case-level tests rather than marginal standard errors for individual accuracies

rationale: Binomial SE at n=750 (and plus-or-minus 3.7 on the dev subset) is given, with the case or run as the unit. Clustering of cases within the 25 scenarios is discussed as case-mix heterogeneity but is not addressed in the uncertainty estimates. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: the proportion of cases on which all k attempts return the same verdict, correct or not
Each system has three independent attempts on all 148 cases.

rationale: pass^k, pass@k and verdict agreement are reported with k=3 on the development subset (Tables 8 and 9). These are all-runs metrics on the final verdict; there is no tool-action sequence or environment-state agreement. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: Opus 4.8 on Claude Code, three explicit reasoning-effort levels over the same 148 development tasks

rationale: Model names carry versions (e.g. GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro) but there are no provider snapshot IDs or release dates, so (i) is scored absent. Reasoning effort is stated only for the ablation, not the headline runs. No harness version or commit is stated for the reported numbers. The ablations also use Opus 4.8 while the leaderboard uses Opus 5. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: SQL Fallback: A capped, read-only SQL interface retained to address coverage gaps in the higher-level clinical tools.

rationale: The benchmark defines a tool interface (MCP). Tools are described by function, with read-only SQL, retrieval tools and a sandboxed shell, which implies reads versus writes. No machine-readable schema is shown and no error or failure return semantics are documented. S5 absent from the packet, so reach cannot be told. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: Parameterized, clinician-verified tools which support common record-retrieval operations across the MIMIC database

rationale: Tools are described as clinician-verified, which is the only verification evidence, with no tests or conformance results. The packet never states explicitly that nothing is simulated or stubbed, and S5 is absent. element_flags 1/3.

searched: S1 (tool environment 3.2, scenarios, evaluation framework), S2-S5 (no chunks). The tools are retrieval, read-only SQL, a computation sandbox and a policy-document reader. No action creates orders, prescriptions, notes or messages, and none changes environment state.

quotes.text: Criteria are graded by an LLM judge against the final report and the logged trajectory together.
Verdict accuracy involves no judge, being a deterministic four-class match against the reference labels.

rationale: Grader inputs are named: deterministic match for verdicts, an LLM judge on report plus trajectory for process, and a rationale for scoring the observable process is given. Judge validation covers regrading stability and inter-judge agreement, not labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: run with web search and fetch disabled, so every system answers from the in-environment patient record and policy corpus alone

rationale: Leakage controls through web access and a credential-isolated tool server are stated. No held-out or private split and no canary or provenance marker is reported. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: Rows are the 25 clinical scenarios, sorted by the unweighted mean over systems given in the last column
exactly 30 for every cell in the grid

rationale: Per-scenario and per-verdict-class results are reported with slice sizes (30 per scenario; class supports yes 50, no 45, lack 39, amb 14). No results by patient demographic subgroup appear, although MIMIC-IV holds demographic fields. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: retrospective, de-identified records from the inpatient, intensive-care, and emergency departments of a single major academic medical center
All Clinical Board reviewers are credentialed PhysioNet users who completed the required training and executed the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement
will be released openly under a permissive license. The patient-linked artifacts, which are derived from MIMIC-IV

rationale: Records are stated as real de-identified MIMIC-IV, governed by credentialed PhysioNet access and a DUA. Data terms (PhysioNet credentialed tier) are stated separately from the permissive licence on non-patient artifacts. element_flags 3/3.
